I farm this small sorghum plot near my home, and the rains here in the North West are not always reliable, so I must be careful with what I spend. I will buy a little fertilizer if I can get it from the agro-dealer, because sorghum gives a poor harvest on our tired soil without it, but I will not use much — just enough for this small plot. I also spread the manure from our small ruminants on the field before planting, which helps the soil. I save my own sorghum seed from last year as my mother taught me, and with my husband and children helping, we can manage most of the work ourselves without paying outside labor.
